items.readable_text:
Content:
For discrete random variables [MATH: X] and [MATH: Y], the conditional expected value of [MATH: X] given [MATH: Y=y] is defined by
[MATH: \textrm E[X|Y=y]=\sum_{x}x f_{X|Y}(x|y)]

Content:
where [MATH: f_{X|Y}(x|y)] is the conditional probability mass function of [MATH: X] given [MATH: Y.]

Content:
This definition is similar to that of [MATH: \textrm{E}[X].] However, we now use the conditional PMF [MATH: f_{X|Y}(x|y)] instead of the marginal PMF [MATH: f_X(x)] in the summation.

Content:
Note the following:

Content:
- The conditional expectation [MATH: \textrm E[X | Y = y]] is (in general) a function of [MATH: y.] This makes intuitive sense. If the distribution of [MATH: X] varies with [MATH: Y,] then the expected value of [MATH: X] for a given [MATH: Y] must vary with the value of [MATH: Y.]
- If [MATH: y] is replaced with a number, then [MATH: \textrm E[X | Y = y]] returns a single value.
- If [MATH: X] and [MATH: Y] are independent, then [MATH: \textrm E[X | Y = y] = \textrm E[X]] for all [MATH: y]. Again, this makes intuitive sense. If the outcome of [MATH: Y] has no influence on the outcome of [MATH: X,] then the distribution of [MATH: X] and, consequently, its mean, is also unaffected by [MATH: Y.]
- We sometimes use the notation [MATH: \mu_{X|y}] to denote [MATH: E[X | Y = y].]

Content:
Finally, we have an analogous definition for [MATH: \textrm E[Y|X=x]\mathbin{:}]

Content:
[MATH: \textrm E[Y|X=x]=\sum_{y}y f_{Y|X}(y|x)]

sections.normalized_html:
The conditional expected value of [MATH: Y] given [MATH: X=x] is defined by

[MATH: \textrm{E}\big[Y \,|\, X=x\big] = \sum_{y} y \, f_{Y | X}(y \,|\, x).]

Therefore, we obtain

[MATH: E[Y|X = 2]|= ∑_(y)yf_{Y|X}(y|2); = 1 ⋅ (2)/(3) + 2 ⋅ (1)/(3); = (4)/(3).]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
For discrete random variables [MATH: X] and [MATH: Y], the conditional expected value of [MATH: X] given [MATH: Y=y] is defined by
[MATH: \textrm E[X|Y=y]=\sum_{x}x f_{X|Y}(x|y)]

Content:
where [MATH: f_{X|Y}(x|y)] is the conditional probability mass function of [MATH: X] given [MATH: Y.]

Content:
This definition is similar to that of [MATH: \textrm{E}[X].] However, we now use the conditional PMF [MATH: f_{X|Y}(x|y)] instead of the marginal PMF [MATH: f_X(x)] in the summation.

Content:
Note the following:

Content:
- The conditional expectation [MATH: \textrm E[X | Y = y]] is (in general) a function of [MATH: y.] This makes intuitive sense. If the distribution of [MATH: X] varies with [MATH: Y,] then the expected value of [MATH: X] for a given [MATH: Y] must vary with the value of [MATH: Y.]
- If [MATH: y] is replaced with a number, then [MATH: \textrm E[X | Y = y]] returns a single value.
- If [MATH: X] and [MATH: Y] are independent, then [MATH: \textrm E[X | Y = y] = \textrm E[X]] for all [MATH: y]. Again, this makes intuitive sense. If the outcome of [MATH: Y] has no influence on the outcome of [MATH: X,] then the distribution of [MATH: X] and, consequently, its mean, is also unaffected by [MATH: Y.]
- We sometimes use the notation [MATH: \mu_{X|y}] to denote [MATH: E[X | Y = y].]

Content:
Finally, we have an analogous definition for [MATH: \textrm E[Y|X=x]\mathbin{:}]

Content:
[MATH: \textrm E[Y|X=x]=\sum_{y}y f_{Y|X}(y|x)]

---

Item 2 — Example: Calculating a Conditional Expected Value Given a Conditional Mass Function

Example Prompt:
| [MATH: y] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 2] |
| [MATH: f_{Y|X}(y \,|\, 2)] | [MATH: \dfrac{2}{3}] | [MATH: \dfrac{1}{3}] |

Find the [MATH: \textrm{E}\big[Y \,|\, X=2\big]] given that the conditional probability mass function [MATH: f_{Y|X}(y \,|\, 2)] is shown in the table above.

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
The conditional expected value of [MATH: Y] given [MATH: X=x] is defined by

[MATH: \textrm{E}\big[Y \,|\, X=x\big] = \sum_{y} y \, f_{Y | X}(y \,|\, x).]

Therefore, we obtain

[MATH: E[Y|X = 2]|= ∑_(y)yf_{Y|X}(y|2); = 1 ⋅ (2)/(3) + 2 ⋅ (1)/(3); = (4)/(3).]
